### Normality and Molarity

* **Normality ($N$):** Defined as the number of gram-equivalents of solute dissolved per liter of solution.
  $$N = \frac{\text{Number of gram equivalents}}{\text{Volume of solution in liters}} = \frac{W \times 1000}{\text{Equivalent weight} \times V_{\text{mL}}}$$

* **Molarity ($M$):** Defined as the number of moles of solute dissolved per liter of solution.
  $$M = \frac{\text{Number of moles}}{\text{Volume of solution in liters}} = \frac{W \times 1000}{\text{Molar mass} \times V_{\text{mL}}}$$
proTip: Keep in mind that Normality depends on the valence/n-factor of the substance, whereas Molarity depends solely on the molecular mass.
